question_type: Linear-trend extrapolation of a 48-month series (Jan 1999-Dec 2002) to Jan 2003, minus an 'actual' Jan 2003 value that the corpus does not contain
decisive_step: What to use as the 'actual' January 2003 value. The series is Table MY-2 'Average Yields of Long-Term Treasury, Corporate and Municipal Bonds', block 'MONTHLY SERIES-AVERAGES OF DAILY OR WEEKLY SERIES', column (2) 'New Aa corporate bonds' (treasury_bulletin_2003_03.txt:2550-2604, 48 rows, no revisions across vintages per the reference's vintage_check). The table ends at Dec 2002 and the next issue says the series was discontinued effective January 2003 (treasury_bulletin_2003_06.txt:2169; reference worklog.md step 2, step 4 'CONCLUSION'). The regression itself is uncontroversial (every cell that computed it got the same fitted line as the reference, calc.py). The reference estimated the missing actual from a Treasury yield plus a spread (worklog.md step 7, solution.json decisions[3], confidence low) and was wrong; every GLM arm in v8, all four cells here, and the reference are wrong, and the two numeric cell answers (one built like the reference, one from a recalled outside figure) are both >25% from the key. The key's convention for the 'actual' is therefore not derivable from the corpus by any arm seen so far.

a.path_summary: Found MY-2 in the March 2003 issue by a[21] and had the 48 training values in view by a[33]-[36]; a printings call for the Jan 2003 cell came back 'no matching row/column' (a[37]-[38]) and it discovered the discontinuation by a[44]-[50]. From about a[65] it entered a fixed cycle of ~14 commands (find_tables 'Aa Corporate Bonds' --rows --years 2003-2003 --all, a python FTS shim query, rg for Moody/Aa/January 2003, printings for the Jan 2003 row, the same calc regression) and repeated that cycle roughly 30 times for the remaining ~55 minutes (a[65]-[849], 423 RUN steps, 426 requests, 53M input tokens). It never submitted; timeout with an empty answer.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Having established that no Jan 2003 value exists (a[50]-[61]), it re-ran the same searches and the same regression ~30 times instead of deciding what to answer; the 'Loops' advice in its own AGENTS.md never took effect (0 mentions of stopping a repeat in 849 steps).
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No cell was right. The reference stopped searching after a bounded hunt (worklog.md step 4 lists the dead ends once), computed the trend once (step 6), chose an explicit estimate for the actual and answered with a flagged low confidence (step 7).

a.saw_correct_evidence: yes (the 48 MY-2 values at a[33]-[36] and the discontinuation note at a[50]; the missing actual is not in the corpus)

smallest_change.change:
printings (and show_table --grep) end-of-series message. When --row names a period later than the last period any issue prints for that table, or earlier than the first, say so instead of the generic 'no matching row/column found', and quote any discontinuation sentence found in the issue after the last printing. What every cell would have seen at its first Jan 2003 lookup (a[37], b call 137, b2[18], c[23]):
printings(row='2003-01', table='MY-2', col='New Aa corporate bonds'): 0 matches
  MY-2 prints periods 1991-01 .. 2002-12; the last issue printing this table is 2003_03 (treasury_bulletin_2003_03.txt:2604 is its last row).
  Later issues do not print MY-2. Note in treasury_bulletin_2003_06.txt:2169: "Effective January 2003, Table MY-2 and Chart MY-B have been discontinued ..."
  The requested period 2003-01 is not printed anywhere in the corpus.
Implementation: the table index already knows first_period/last_period per part and the issues per table id (otables.py find_page uses them); add a grep of the next issue's section text for 'discontinued' within ~50 lines of the table id.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: no: it only replaces a dead-end message with a definite one; it adds nothing when the period exists.
smallest_change.confidence: low for correctness (no cell or arm has found the key's convention for the missing actual); high that it would have ended the hunt that consumed 60 min in a, ~23 min in b and b2, since all three loops were searches for this one absent value

alternatives.change: Enforced loop guard instead of an advisory note: when a command's text and output hash equal a previous call's, do not re-execute it; return one line '[harness:loop] identical to call N (output suppressed)'; after the 5th such suppression in a row, insert '[harness:loop] you have re-run 5 commands with known output; submit the best candidate now or state in one line what value is missing' and, for text-static cells, apply the same rule (it needs no submit machinery). a's 30 cycles, b's ~88 show_table repeats and b2's ~45 printings-loop repeats (each ~78 KB) would have been cut to a few calls and the compactions avoided.
alternatives.why_not_first: It treats the symptom; the cells looped because the tool kept returning an ambiguous 'no match' for a value that does not exist. But it is the change with the largest cost effect on this question and applies to every question with an absent value.

alternatives.change: answer_count should not reject a non-numeric answer when the trajectory contains an end-of-series or discontinuation message for the requested period; instead print a finding 'the question asks for 1 value; the corpus does not print <period> for <table>: answer with your best documented estimate and say what it assumes, or keep' with an offer built from the last printed value. b2's honest 'not computable' at b2[262] was rejected with no offer and it fabricated an estimate two calls later.
alternatives.why_not_first: The key is numeric, so an honest non-answer is still graded wrong; this improves behaviour, not the score.

alternatives.change: Add: 'If the period or value the question asks for is not printed in any issue, do not keep searching: state in your working what is missing, choose one documented proxy from the corpus (for example the last printed value or the nearest published series plus the last printed spread), compute with it, and answer that number.'
alternatives.why_not_first: Cells a and b2 had text telling them to stop repeating commands and ignored it dozens of times; a sentence is unlikely to end a hunt that the tool output keeps re-opening, and it still cannot pick the key's convention.

fix.why_not_text: Cell a had the 'Loops' sentence and repeated a 14-command cycle ~30 times for 55 minutes; b2 had it plus loop-guard notes and repeated a 78 KB printings loop ~45 times. The behaviour was driven by what the tools printed (a bare 'no matching row/column' that reads like a lookup mistake rather than an absent value), so the fix has to change that output or enforce the stop.
fix.irreducible: For correctness, yes as far as any arm shows: the actual Jan 2003 value of this series is not in the corpus (discontinued effective Jan 2003), the reference solver's corpus-anchored estimate (low confidence, reviewer 'uncertain') and b2's identical construction are >25% from the key, b's recalled outside figure is also >25% off, and all three v8 arms failed. The key's convention (an outside series, a different regression, or a different reading of 'actual') cannot be inferred from the documents. The adapter changes above reduce cost and improve honesty; they do not recover the answer.

notes: (1) This question is the single largest cost item of the pilot: a 3600 s / 426 requests / 53M input tokens with no answer; b and b2 ~1400 s each with one compaction. All of it was spent hunting for a value the corpus does not contain, after each cell had already read the discontinuation note (a[50], b[33], b2[26], c[57]). (2) The advisory loop guard is capped (loop_notes_max 3) and names the command but does not stop it; b repeated the named command ~85 more times, b2 ~40 more. (3) printings per cell on a 48-month window produces ~78 KB; a whole-column mode (`printings --table MY-2 --col ... --rows 1999-01..2002-12` printing one line per period with first/latest issue and a 'no revisions' summary) would cut that to ~50 lines and is what the text's 'printings for every cell' advice implicitly asks for. (4) The answer_count rule rejected an honest 'not computable' (b2[262]) with no offer; the model then fabricated. If v10 keeps submit checks, a non-numeric answer after an end-of-series finding should get an offer, not a bare rejection. (5) Environment friction seen in three cells: zsh treats '===$f' as an '=' expansion (b[31], b2[220], c[55]); rg returns exit 1 on no match, which the digest shows as an error; the python officeqa shim prints object reprs (b[6]-[10], a's 66 shim calls). (6) The regression is robust to the x-encoding (reference calc.py checked 1..48 vs 0..47); b2[243] briefly worried about it, no cell got it wrong.
